Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap - audit logs & data access (Finco)

Hi Tom - thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps on the audit logs / access evidence we discussed:

- What we'll provide: a time-bounded export of inference audit logs showing who accessed what and when, an access-controls manifest, and a short readme describing retention and export formats.
- Format options: CSV (flat rows) or JSON (nested). Let us know which you prefer - CSV is typically easiest for ingestion.
- Retention/PII: we can provide raw user identifiers or hashed identifiers; we can also redact fields flagged as PII. Please confirm your preference.
- Time window: please confirm the date range you need. We can run exports for the last 90 days by default.
- Delivery: target delivering the package via secure link within 48-72 hours after we confirm scope.

Next steps: can you confirm (A) exact fields you need in the audit export (timestamp timezone, user id, action, resource, request_id, model_id, token_count), (B) desired redaction policy for PII, and (C) who on your security/procurement team should be on the delivery?

I'm looping in Marissa (Security) and Aditya (TAM) to own the export and format.

Thanks - Laura

--
Laura Bennett

Thanks Laura - helpful recap. A few clarifications so we can scope the request on our side:

1) Fields we need in the audit export (preferred order):
   - timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC)
   - user_id (or hashed user id)
   - action (e.g., generate, read, export, kv_access)
   - resource (model or dataset identifier)
   - request_id / correlation_id
   - model_id / model_version
   - token_count (input + output)
   - response_hash (optional)

2) PII handling: we prefer user_id to be hashed (SHA-256) and for any free-text outputs flagged as PII to be redacted. If Redwood redacts, please document the redaction rules.

3) Export delivery: Secure S3 presigned URL or encrypted attachment via secure portal are fine. Procurement prefers S3. We need this in 3 business days if possible.

4) Please confirm whether the logs will show who accessed KV/cache vs who executed inference requests (we need both if possible).

CCing our procurement contact - they'll track the evidence delivery.

--Tom
Security Engineering, Finco Bank

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap - audit logs & data access (Finco)

Hi Tom / Laura - thanks for the details. We can deliver the evidence package as requested. Plan below:

1) Export format: CSV with UTF-8 and a small accompanying JSON manifest describing schema and redaction rules. Sample CSV columns: timestamp_utc, user_hash_sha256, action, resource, request_id, model_id, token_count, response_hash, redaction_flag

2) PII/redaction: we will hash user identifiers with SHA-256. For model outputs, we'll include a redaction_flag per row and will remove/replace obviously sensitive fields (emails, SSNs) as per our redaction policy. The manifest will include exact rules.

3) KV/access visibility: our runtime logs include separate event types for kv_read / kv_write and inference_generate; both will be included in the action column. We'll include an extra column event_type to make filtering easier.

4) Retention & timezone: timestamps will be ISO 8601 UTC. Retention metadata will be included in the manifest (created_at, retention_policy_days). Our default export will cover 2026-03-01 to 2026-06-24 unless you confirm a different range.

5) Delivery: We'll upload files to a secure S3 bucket and provide presigned read-only URLs. Files we plan to include: fincobank_audit_log_export_2026-06-24.csv, fincobank_access_controls_manifest_2026-06-24.csv, redwood_audit_logs_readme_2026-06-24.txt.

We aim to have the package available by EOD Friday (within 48 hours). If you need a stricter SLA, let us know.

Regards - Marissa
